questions.question_text: Which of the following expenses is classified as a **fixed expense** in a personal or household budget?

options.why: Classifies a non-essential leisure subscription as a fixed expense.
Classifies discretionary food and hospitality spending as fixed.
Classifies non-essential clothing/footwear as fixed.

questions.solution_text: Compulsory third-party insurance is a mandatory, recurring contractual commitment required to drive a vehicle, making it a fixed expense.

questions.question_text: Ethan spends \$65 per week on public transport fares. What is his total annual transport expenditure (based on a $52$-week year)?

options.why: Multiplies by $12$ months instead of $52$ weeks.
Multiplies by $26$ fortnights instead of $52$ weeks.
Multiplies by $48$ assuming $4$ weeks per month.

questions.question_text: An individual has an annual net income of \$54 000 and total annual expenses of \$48 600. What is their monthly budget balance?

options.why: Stops at the annual surplus of \$5400 and forgets to divide by $12$ to convert it to a monthly balance.
Divides correctly by $12$ but subtracts the wrong way round, taking income from expenses and so reporting the balance as a shortfall.
Subtracts income from expenses instead of expenses from income and also leaves the figure annual instead of dividing by $12$.
Calculates the monthly surplus but forgets to convert to an annual amount ($\times 12$).
Subtracts only fixed expenses from income before annualising ($(\$4200 - \$2500) \times 12$).
Multiplies monthly surplus by $26$ fortnights instead of $12$ months.

questions.question_text: A household's essential living expenses are \$4500 per month. How much should they set aside in an emergency fund to cover $6$ months of living expenses?

options.why: Calculates an emergency fund for $3$ months instead of $6$ months.
Calculates an emergency fund for $12$ months (one full year).
Calculates $5$ months of expenses instead of $6$ months.

questions.question_text: A worker's monthly income is \$3200 and their monthly expenses are \$3450 (Fixed: \$2300, Discretionary: \$1150), leaving a monthly deficit of \$250. If fixed expenses cannot be changed, how much must monthly discretionary spending be reduced to balance the budget?

options.why: Gives the new target discretionary budget instead of the amount by which it must be reduced.
Eliminates all discretionary spending completely rather than just covering the deficit.
Calculates the annual deficit instead of the required monthly reduction.

questions.question_text: Oliver earns \$850 per week. His expenses are: Rent \$310/week, Groceries \$180/week, Electricity \$360/quarter ($4$ quarters/year), Car running costs \$220/fortnight, and Entertainment \$120/fortnight. What is Oliver's annual budget balance?

options.why: Omits the quarterly electricity expense from the annual total.
Calculates fortnight expenses with $\times 12$ instead of $\times 26$.
Calculates weekly rent and groceries using $48$ weeks instead of $52$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$850 \times 52 = \$44\,200$
$\text{Rent} = \$310 \times 52 = \$16\,120$
$\text{Groceries} = \$180 \times 52 = \$9360$
$\text{Electricity} = \$360 \times 4 = \$1440$
$\text{Car costs} = \$220 \times 26 = \$5720$
$\text{Entertainment} = \$120 \times 26 = \$3120$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$16\,120 + \$9360 + \$1440 + \$5720 + \$3120 = \$35\,760$
$\text{Annual balance} = \$44\,200 - \$35\,760$
$= \$8440\text{ surplus}$

questions.question_text: An individual earns a net weekly income of \$750 and has fixed annual expenses of \$26 000. If they aim to achieve an annual savings surplus of \$5200, what is the maximum average weekly discretionary spending they can afford?

options.why: Calculates total weekly surplus capacity without subtracting the \$5200 savings target.
Identifies the weekly savings target rather than the weekly discretionary spending.
Adds the savings target instead of subtracting it from available surplus capacity.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$750 \times 52 = \$39\,000$
$\text{Max total expenses} = \$39\,000 - \$5200 = \$33\,800$
$\text{Max annual discretionary spending} = \$33\,800 - \$26\,000 = \$7800$
$\text{Weekly discretionary budget} = \dfrac{\$7800}{52}$
$= \$150\text{ per week}$
